samples.summary: Header/footer drag selection is the one pointer gesture not routed through the new link snap, so #1038's "a partial link selection snaps whole" rule does not hold inside headers/footers
samples.evidence: `updateDragSelection`'s header/footer branch still calls `this.selection.setRange({ anchor: this.selection.range.anchor, focus: pos })` directly (text-editor.ts:2232), while the body branch (2360) and the mousedown word/paragraph/shift+click paths (1990, 2000, 2016, 2056, 2068, 2074) all go through `setSnappedRange`. Because those mousedown paths are shared with the header/footer edit context, a shift+click or double-click inside a header DOES snap a link whole but a drag in the same header does not — the pre-#1038 partial-link state stays reachable there, and the two gestures now disagree within one region. Headers do support links (packages/docs/test/view/hf-cursor-screen-rect.test.ts drives `insertLink` in the header context). The task plan only scoped "drag update + shift+click extend (body and in-cell)", so this is an acknowledged-but-unstated hole rather than an oversight, hence minor.

samples.summary: `anchorComesFirst` reinvents endpoint ordering in a weaker form than the layout-free ordering `visitRangeSlices` already performs, so the snap silently declines in cases the repo can already order
samples.evidence: `anchorComesFirst` orders same-block ranges by offset and cross-block ranges by `doc.getBlockIndex`, giving up (`undefined` → no snap) for two blocks inside one table cell or in header/footer. `packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:160-204` already solves exactly this without a `DocumentLayout`: it detects the "cross-block inside one cell" case via `doc.blockParentMap` and orders by the cell's own block list, and it normalizes cell endpoints to their parent table block before comparing `getBlockIndex`. That logic is inline rather than exported, so this is not a literal duplicate call site, but the new helper is a second, less capable answer to the same question and the cost is a user-visible gap: a drag spanning two paragraphs inside a table cell that ends mid-link is left partially covering the link, the state #1038 is about. Extracting/reusing the range-slices ordering would close it and keep one answer.

samples.summary: Only the docs editor's *selection* branch got the in-place href rewrite; the mirrored text-box editor's selection branch was left as a bare `applyInlineStyle`, so the two editors now diverge on the very behaviour the shared helper exists to keep in step
samples.evidence: editor.ts:3612 adds `linkRunCoveringRange` + `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace` to the selection branch, so a selected self-labelled link has its display text follow the new URL. text-box-editor.ts:1187-1193 still does `docStore.snapshot(); doc.applyInlineStyle(range, { href: url })` for a selection, so in the slides/board text-box the same gesture leaves the stale URL as display text. The task plan's own justification for putting these helpers in link-run.ts is "shared so the two editors cannot diverge (the reason #580 shared `findLinkRunAt`)" (docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-link-text-and-snap-todo.md:15-17), and the caret branch WAS mirrored (text-box-editor.ts:1205). Cost is contained today because Part B's pointer snap is docs-only and slides exposes no link UI beyond `api.insertLink` (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:634), which is why this is minor rather than major.

samples.summary: The "is the caret still on the link I opened" rule is implemented in the React popover against `getLinkAtCursor`, a second independent link-at-caret implementation, rather than in the editor API that owns link semantics
samples.evidence: The guard `editingHref !== null && editor.getLinkAtCursor() !== editingHref` encodes knowledge of `insertLink`'s branch semantics (that a caret outside a link inserts the URL as text, and a caret in another link rewrites that one) in the frontend component. `editor.getLinkAtCursor` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3713-3735) is a hand-rolled walk over `block.inlines` that re-derives `findLinkRunAt`'s tie-break by comment ("matching findLinkRunAt's tie-break") instead of calling it — pre-existing duplication that this change makes load-bearing: if the two tie-breaks ever drift, Apply refuses on a link the popover is legitimately editing, or permits an edit to a neighbouring link. A docs-side API (e.g. `editLinkAtCursor(url, expectedHref)`) would keep the rule next to `findLinkRunAt`/`linkRunCoveringRange`. Behaviour as shipped matches the plan, so minor.

samples.summary: A new selection-model rule ("a hyperlink is an atomic selection unit") plus a new `Selection` field are recorded only in task docs; no design doc under docs/design/ was added or updated, unlike the merged-cell precedent it explicitly follows
samples.evidence: The change adds `Selection.rawAnchor` (selection.ts:701) and a new invariant that pointer selections are grown to cover links whole, with knock-on semantics the plan itself lists as accepted consequences (delete/type-over destroys the whole link, ⌘B restyles it whole, comment `quotedText` widens — docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-link-text-and-snap-todo.md:60-64). No file under docs/design/ mentions this: `docs/design/docs/docs.md:274` still describes selection.ts as "range tracking and highlight rendering", and grep finds no docs/design page covering hyperlink editing semantics at all. The analogous rule for merged cells IS documented (`docs/design/docs/tables/docs-table-copy-paste.md:33`, `expandCellRangeForMerges`). CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16/56-62 asks for a design doc for non-trivial/data-model changes, folded into the canonical subsystem doc rather than a parallel file. Cost stays inside the codebase (behaviour is as specified), so minor; the fix is a short section in docs/design/docs/docs.md, not a new parallel doc.

samples.summary: Word- and paragraph-select snapping is scope beyond the task plan's stated Part B wiring (drag + shift+click)
samples.evidence: The plan wires the snap at "drag update + shift+click extend (body and in-cell)" (todo:53-54); the diff additionally routes triple-click paragraph select (2056, and the in-cell 1990) and double-click word select (2068, in-cell 2000) through `setSnappedRange`. The double-click case is well argued in-comment (`getWordRange` splits a URL at punctuation), and paragraph select is only there for the raw anchor, so this reads as justified follow-through rather than drift — noting it only because it changes double-click behaviour inside URL-labelled links (a word is no longer selectable there) without the plan or a design doc saying so.

searchedFor: grep insertLink in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts and text-box-editor.ts
grep linkTextFollowsHref call sites (only caret branches)
finding.summary: Part A ('a URL-derived display text follows the new URL') is implemented only in insertLink's caret branch; the selection branch still only rewrites href, so the defect survives on the most natural flow after Part B
finding.evidence: insertLink's selection branch (editor.ts:3582-3611) does `doc.applyInlineStyle(range, { href: url })` and nothing else — no `linkTextFollowsHref` check, no text replacement. Part B now makes 'the whole link is selected' the normal result of dragging over a link (expandRangeForLinks snaps a partial drag out to run.start..run.end). A user who selects a self-labelled link (text === href) and presses ⌘K / uses the toolbar therefore still ends up with the old URL as visible text and a new href — exactly the reported #1038 Part A symptom, reachable in one gesture. The task plan (docs/tasks/active/20260907-docs-link-text-and-snap-todo.md:18) scopes the fix to the caret branch only, and the same gap exists in text-box-editor.ts. Cost: the stated outcome does not hold for selection-driven URL edits.

verdict.reason: The finding claims insertLink's selection branch in packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts only rewrites href with no Part A ("URL-derived display text follows the new URL") handling. It does have it. At editor.ts:3607-3631 the selection branch calls linkRunCoveringRange(doc, range) and, when the selection exactly covers a single link run, delegates to rewriteLinkHrefInPlace(doc, covered.block, covered.run, url, snapshot) — the identical shared helper used by the caret branch at editor.ts:3663 — which evaluates linkTextFollowsHref (link-run.ts:94, defined at link-run.ts:67) and replaces the display text when it was URL-derived (link-run.ts:101-112), then re-points the stored selection and caret (editor.ts:3617-3626) and returns before the plain applyInlineStyle fallback at 3634. linkRunCoveringRange's doc comment (link-run.ts:115-124) states it exists precisely because expandRangeForLinks (text-editor.ts:2383) makes "whole link selected" the normal result of a drag, and that this case must behave like the caret path (#1038). So the exact user flow the finding says is broken — drag over a self-labelled link, press ⌘K — is the case that is explicitly handled. The reviewer's quoted line window (3582-3611) stops one line short of the branch it says is missing. The passing mention of text-box-editor.ts:1187 is a different location covered by its own separate finding and does not support this finding's named claim.

finding.summary: Link snapping is wired only into drag and shift+click; double-click word select and triple-click still produce a partially covered link
finding.evidence: expandRangeForLinks is reached only via setSnappedRange, called from the two shift+click paths (2016, 2067) and updateDragSelection (2353). The double-click word-select paths (`getWordRange` → `this.selection.setRange({ anchor, focus })` at text-editor.ts:2000 for cells and 2052/2061 for body) and triple-click still store an unsnapped range, so double-clicking a word inside `https://example.com` leaves a partial link selection — the state Part B declares impossible ('a link behaves as an atomic unit'), and applying ⌘B or ⌘K there splits the link. The task plan limits wiring to 'drag update + shift+click extend', so this may be an accepted scope cut, but nothing in the diff records it (unlike the deliberate shift+arrow comment).

verdict.reason: The finding claims double-click word-select and triple-click bypass link snapping by calling `this.selection.setRange({ anchor, focus })` directly. The code does the opposite: all four paths route through `setSnappedRange`, the sole caller of `expandRangeForLinks`. Body double-click at text-editor.ts:2068 uses `this.setSnappedRange({ anchor, focus }, anchor)` and carries a comment at 2059-2062 naming the exact `https://example.com` scenario the finding says is unhandled. Body triple-click at 2056, cell triple-click at 1990, and cell double-click at 2000 likewise use `setSnappedRange`. The `raw` parameter of `setSnappedRange` is documented at 2375-2379 as existing specifically for "word and paragraph select" — the gestures alleged to be unwired. The remaining bare `selection.setRange` calls at 2037 and 2079 are single-click caret placement (collapsed range, nothing to snap). Test `link-snap-pointer.test.ts:260` asserts "double-clicking inside a link selects the whole link". The quoted evidence does not match the working tree; the cited lines fall inside the range the reviewer says they read.
